why: Use of 54 to 118 rolls per person a year, rolls of 20 to 50 metres and roll prices of $0.40 to $0.90 against costs of $0.20 to $0.50 are believable toilet tissue figures.
About 1.1 million employees across the city's households, most of them not yet contacted by a dental insurer and with the contacted ones concentrated at large employers, is believable.
Market shares of 0.4% to 6.8% in toehold countries and profit margins of 10% to 42% are believable for a games publisher, even if the top margin is high.

The cumulative curve reaches 100% of all developing-market pet food sales at market 41 and stays flat, so markets 42 to 50 and every other developing country together have under 0.05% (about $18m) of a $37bn market, while market 41 alone has about 0.3% (about $110m), a cliff no real tail of national markets shows.
Monthly revenue of about $1.9m across 18 showrooms (about $1.2m per showroom a year), a 15% rise in timber prices and a 15% fall in margin index are believable.
Toll income of £15m to £44m a road against maintenance spend of £1.8m to £5.8m is believable for a concession toll road operator.

64,000 out-of-hours consultations for 35,000 pets, £3.4m of fixed cost plus £45 a visit, and group pet counts that add to 35k with cost per pet falling from Group A to Group E are consistent and believable.
An industrial robot market of about €0.5bn split across electronics, car and food packaging customers is believable for a national market, with modest past growth and faster forecast growth.
Tyre sales of $480m through 960 garages (about $0.4m to $1.0m per garage a year), shares adding to 100% and warranty claims of 3% to 6% are believable.
Exit surveys of 1,340 and 910 bank customers with rating distributions that each add to 100% are believable.
